journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: From Education to Technology: A Multi Criteria Analysis of Nursing Shortage Solutions Using the EDAS Method
abstract: This study uses the Entropy-Based Distribution Algorithm (EDAS) method to analyse various strategies to address the global nursing shortage. The research evaluated five main approaches: expanding educational programs, encouraging nursing employment, recruiting international nurses, using technology, and increasing nurse retention. The analysis examined four important factors: projected shortages, workforce growth, vacancy rates, and educational barriers. The results show that expanding educational programs emerged as the most effective strategy, ranking first with an ASi value of 0.95031, followed by encouraging nursing employment (ASi = 0.87840). Nurse retention ranked third (ASI = 0.39529), while technology use and international recruitment ranked fourth and fifth with ASI values of 0.23399 and 0.21791, respectively. While technology showed promising workforce growth (164.00) and contributed to the expansion of the international recruitment workforce (121.00), both strategies faced significant implementation challenges. The findings suggest that a comprehensive approach that prioritizes educational expansion and career incentives, supported by retention strategies, is most effect

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Evaluating the Impact of a School Based Compassionate Citizenship Program: A Statistical Analysis
abstract: In an increasingly complex social and environmental context, fostering social responsibility, environmental consciousness, empathy, and active citizenship among young people is essential. This study presents a statistical evaluation of the Compassionate Citizenship Program (CCP) 2025–26, a school-based intervention designed to promote these values and behaviours among students. The effectiveness of the CCP is assessed by examining changes in students’ social awareness, environmental consciousness, civic participation, and attitudes toward social responsibility. A three-stage longitudinal survey design is employed, with data collected before the intervention (Pre), during implementation (Mid), and after completion of the program (Post). A mixed-methods approach is adopted, integrating quantitative analyses, including frequency distributions, percentage analysis, comparative analysis and chi-square tests of association, with qualitative analysis of coded student responses. The paper outlines the research design, data structure, and analytical framework used to evaluate the program’s impact across cognitive, affective and behavioural domains. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Evaluating First Aid Training Alternatives Using Weighted Sum Model: A Comparative Analysis of Traditional and Digital Approaches
abstract: This study evaluates different first aid training alternatives using the Weighted Sum Model (WSM) to determine the most effective option for acquiring first aid knowledge and skills. The research analyzes five alternatives: Basic First Aid Training Kit, Online First Aid Course, Community First Aid Workshop, Certified Training Program, and First Aid App with Tutorials. These options were assessed across four key parameters: Comprehensiveness (C), Accessibility (A), Practical Training (P), and Complexity (Cx), with equal weights of 0.25 assigned to each criterion. The methodology involved normalizing the dataset and calculating weighted scores to rank the alternatives based on their overall performance. The analysis revealed that the First Aid App with Tutorials achieved the highest preference score (0.87500), ranking first due to its exceptional performance in Accessibility, Practical Training, and Complexity, despite lower scores in Comprehensiveness. The Basic First Aid Training Kit ranked second (0.70417), followed by the Online First Aid Course (0.67500), Community First Aid Workshop (0.56875), and Certified Training Program (0.55476). journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Integrating Cultural Aspects into Assessment and Monitoring Using ARAS Method
abstract: In today’s multicultural environment, integrating cultural awareness into assessment and monitoring processes is essential to promote fairness, inclusiveness, and effective service delivery. This study examines the importance of embedding cultural considerations throughout every stage of assessment and monitoring, from designing instruments to interpreting results. Existing research highlights several strategies that strengthen cultural responsiveness, including developing culturally appropriate assessment tools, recognizing cultural influences during data collection and interpretation, and maintaining active engagement with communities. Embedding cultural competence improves the quality and reliability of collected information, helps identify disparities, and supports the creation of interventions suited to diverse populations. Effective assessment requires professionals to understand both their own cultural perspectives and those of the individuals being evaluated. Addressing language differences through translated materials and interpreter support, while adapting communication methods to cultural expectations, further enhances accuracy. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Visual Learning for Better Outcomes: Role of Infographics on Enhancing Achievement in Business Studies Among Higher Secondary School Students
abstract: The increasing integration of digital technologies in education has highlighted the need for innovative instructional strategies that enhance students' engagement and academic achievement. Although infographics have emerged as an effective visual learning tool for simplifying complex information, empirical evidence regarding their effectiveness in Commerce education, particularly in Business Studies at the higher secondary level, remains limited. The present study examined the effectiveness of infographics in enhancing the academic achievement of higher secondary school students in Business Studies. A quasi-experimental control group pretest post-test design was adopted. The sample consisted of 80 Grade XII Commerce students from two higher secondary schools in Alappuzha District Among 80 students,40 students were selected randomly to form experimental group and 40 students were randomly selected to form control group. The experimental group received instruction through a researcher-developed infographic-based instructional package, while the control group was taught using the prevailing activity method. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Majuli’s Mask Art and Cultural Tourism: Issues of Sustainability and Preservation
abstract: Majuli, the world’s largest inhabited river island situated in Assam, India, represents a unique confluence of cultural heritage, traditional craftsmanship and religious practices. Among its most celebrated cultural expressions is the art of mask-making (Mukha Shilpa), which emerged within the Neo-Vaishnavite movement initiated by Srimanta Sankardeva during the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. These masks are extensively used in Bhaona performances and other religious activities conducted in the Satras of Majuli. In recent decades, cultural tourism has increased significantly, bringing economic opportunities and greater visibility to the island’s artistic traditions. However, the growing commercialization of mask art, environmental degradation, riverbank erosion, climate change and the declining participation of younger generations have raised serious concerns regarding sustainability and preservation. This study examines the historical and cultural significance of Majuli’s mask art, evaluates the role of cultural tourism in promoting local development and identifies major sustainability and preservation challenges. The paper further explores strategies for safeguarding this inta

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: A Decision Support Framework for Performance Evaluation of Indian Technical Institutions using MOORA Method
abstract: ndian technical institutions form the foundation of the country’s advanced education system and are recognized internationally for their strong academic standards, experienced faculty, and modern infrastructure. These institutions attract students from India and abroad by creating an environment that supports academic achievement and professional growth. A defining feature of technical education in India is its focus on experiential learning through internships, industry partnerships, research projects, and practical applications that strengthen technical expertise and analytical abilities. These institutions also act as centres of innovation and research by promoting studies in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, biotechnology, and renewable energy. Through incubation centres, technology parks, and entrepreneurial initiatives, students and researchers are encouraged to develop innovative solutions and startup ventures. Collaborative research involving industry, government agencies, and international institutions further accelerates technological advancement and knowledge exchange. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: From Margins to Mainstream: The Rise of BJP in Assam’s Political Landscape
abstract: The emergence of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) as the dominant political force in Assam represents one of the most significant transformations in the state’s electoral history. Once a marginal political party with limited organizational presence, the BJP has successfully expanded its electoral base through a combination of identity politics, strategic alliances, welfare-oriented governance, organizational strengthening, and effective political communication. This article examines the factors responsible for the BJP’s rise from the political margins to the mainstream of Assam’s electoral landscape. Using qualitative research based on secondary sources, including books, journal articles, election reports, government publications, and newspaper archives, the study explores the interplay of regional identity, nationalism, coalition politics, anti-incumbency sentiment, and welfare policies in shaping voter preferences. The analysis demonstrates that the BJP’s success cannot be attributed to a single factor; rather, it is the result of a multidimensional electoral strategy that combines ideological mobilization with pragmatic political alliances and governance initiatives. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Beyond Poverty: How Parental Education Shapes Children's Brain Structure and Academic Achievement in the First Eight Years
abstract: Early childhood education (birth to age 8) is a critical developmental period characterized by rapid brain growth and high capacity for change, which lays the foundation for lifelong health, well-being, and educational success. This study examines the multifaceted relationships between parental education, family income, and child development outcomes. Methods: A cross-sectional analysis was conducted involving 389 children aged 4–22 years using multiple assessment instruments, including the Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scale-Short Form and the Family Literacy Environmental Scale. Bivariate and multiple regression models were used to analyze the relationships between socioeconomic factors and child outcomes. Background questionnaires collected data on maternal education, family characteristics, and duration of childcare. Academic achievement tests were administered by trained raters in controlled school settings in the fall of 1991–92. Research Importance: The findings revealed that parental education had a strong and consistent direct effect on children’s cognitive and academic outcomes compared with family income alone. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Meranaw Culture-Based Instruction on the Conceptual Understanding of Grade 9 Students in Mathematics
abstract: This study determined the effectiveness of Meranaw Culture-Based Instruction integrated with the 5I’s Learning Path in improving the conceptual understanding of Grade 9 students in Mathematics. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed. The quantitative phase utilized a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design involving 90 Grade 9 students divided equally into experimental and control groups. The experimental group received Meranaw culture-based instruction while the control group received conventional instruction. A researcher-developed Conceptual Understanding Test measured students’ achievement, while interviews, classroom observations, and reflection journals were conducted to explain the quantitative results. Descriptive statistics and Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) were used to analyze the quantitative data, whereas thematic analysis was used to analyze the qualitative findings. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Jyoti Prasad Agarwala's Contribution to Assamese Literature: A Lasting Legacy of Creativity and Cultural Revival
abstract: Jyoti Prasad Agarwala occupies a distinguished place in the history of Assamese literature and culture. Popularly known as "Rupkonwar," he was a multifaceted personality whose contributions extended beyond literature to music, drama, cinema and social reform. His literary works emerged during a crucial period in Assam's history when questions of cultural identity, nationalism and social progress were becoming increasingly significant. Through his poems, plays, songs and essays, Agarwala sought to inspire the Assamese people to embrace their cultural heritage while simultaneously encouraging them to participate in the broader movement for national awakening. His writings combined artistic excellence with social commitment and reflected a deep concern for humanity, freedom and justice. The present study examines the nature and significance of Agarwala's contribution to Assamese literature and evaluates his role in the cultural revival of Assam. The paper also explores the major themes found in his literary works, including nationalism, humanism, and love of nature, social reform and cultural consciousness. title: Evaluation of Cultural Considerations in Assessment and Monitoring using FUZZY ARAS Method
abstract: Assessment and monitoring, cultural awareness is essential to uphold fairness and precision among varied demographic groups. It’s imperative for professionals to exhibit cultural proficiency, grasping not only their own cultural context but also that of those being assessed. Overcoming language barriers involves providing translated materials and interpreter services, while adapting communication styles to align with cultural norms is vital. Factors like family dynamics, religious beliefs, socioeconomic status, and biases significantly influence how individuals engage with assessment methods. Collaborating with community leaders and organizations enables professionals to cultivate culturally attuned assessment and monitoring techniques, acknowledging and honouring the diverse range of human experiences. Cultural factors are pivotal in assessment and monitoring research, ensuring the accuracy, fairness, and efficacy of measurement tools across diverse populations. By recognizing and addressing cultural distinctions, researchers can refine assessment and monitoring procedures, resulting in more dependable data and findings. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Home, Exile and Hybridity: A Post-Colonial Reading of Anita Desai's Bye-Bye Blackbird
abstract: Anita Desai’s Bye-Bye Blackbird canvases the psychological and cultural dislocation of Indian immigrants in 1960s Britain. This paper attempts to examine the text through a post-colonial lens, focusing on the diasporic experiences of Indian immigrants in the then Britain. By exploring the disheveled concepts of home, exile and hybridity, the study analyses how national identity is constructed and deconstructed within the domestic and public spheres. Through the characters of Admit, Dev, Sarah, this paper demonstrates that "home" is not a fixed geographical location but a fluid, highly politicized psychological state. Anita Desai argues that the immigrant condition is not a binary opposition between East and West. It is actually a condition where identity is repeatedly negotiated. The research highlights how the immigrant experience equivocates between the desire for assimilation and the inescapable reality of cultural alienation, ultimately revealing the profound psychological toll of displacement.

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: The Global Reader and the Cultural Universalism of Personal Legend
abstract: This paper explores The Alchemist as a globally resonant text that transcends cultural, linguistic, and geographical boundaries through its central concept of the “Personal Legend.” Written by Paulo Coelho, the novel presents a universal narrative of self-discovery, destiny, and spiritual fulfillment that appeals to a diverse international readership. The study examines how the idea of the Personal Legend functions as a culturally adaptable philosophy, enabling readers from varied backgrounds to interpret and internalize its message within their own socio-cultural contexts. By analyzing the novel’s symbolic language, allegorical structure, and spiritual motifs, the paper highlights how Coelho constructs a form of cultural universalism that bridges differences and fosters a shared human experience. Furthermore, it investigates the role of globalization in the novel’s widespread reception and its impact on shaping a “global reader” who engages with literature beyond traditional cultural confines. Ultimately, the paper argues that The Alchemist exemplifies how literature can act as a unifying force, promoting cross-cultural understanding and emphasizing the universality of human aspir

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Examining the Dynamics of Electoral Coalitions in Indian Politics A Case Study Analysis
abstract: Electoral alliances hold significant sway over the dynamics of Indian politics, exerting considerable influence over outcomes in both national and regional arenas. This scholarly investigation endeavors to delve deeply into the complexities surrounding these alliances within the Indian political landscape, examining their establishment, endurance, and effects on governance. By conducting an extensive examination of varied regions and political scenarios, this study aims to reveal the key drivers behind coalition building, the intricate negotiations at play, and the resultant implications for political stability and the execution of policies. Through an examination of historical data, electoral patterns, and qualitative perspectives from relevant stakeholders, this paper endeavors to offer significant insights into the evolving landscape of coalition politics in India and its repercussions on the nation’s democratic structure. This research endeavor strives to enrich the current body of knowledge on Indian politics by presenting a nuanced comprehension of the impact of electoral coalitions on governance and political results. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Indian knowledge Systems helping the mankind in the present generation
abstract: The Indian Knowledge System (IKS) is a collection of knowledge and practices that have developed in India over thousands of years. It includes many areas such as philosophy, mathematics, commerce, medicine (like Ayurveda), arts, architecture, farming, and understanding nature. This traditional wisdom was passed down through generations and has helped people live in harmony with nature and society. Today, in the 21st century, there is a growing interest in bringing this ancient knowledge together with modern science and technology. By combining the old with the new, we can create better and more sustainable ways to live. For example, using traditional farming methods along with modern tools can protect the environment and produce healthy food. Similarly, using Ayurveda along with modern healthcare can improve overall well-being. This paper throws light on how Indian Knowledge Systems are being brought back into use and how they are being combined with today’s scientific innovations. It also looks at what this combination means for areas like education, health, commerce, environment, and sustainable development. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Historical Perspectives on Banking System in Kerala
abstract: The banking system in Kerala has evolved through a rich historical trajectory shaped by indigenous practices, colonial influences, and post-independence reforms. Early financial activities were rooted in traditional institutions such as moneylenders, chit funds, and temple-based treasuries, which catered to local economic needs. During the colonial period, the introduction of modern banking by European agencies and the establishment of early native banks marked a significant transformation. The 20th century witnessed the emergence of prominent Kerala-based banks, fostering regional economic development and financial inclusion. Post-independence nationalization and regulatory frameworks further strengthened the banking infrastructure, expanding rural outreach and priority sector lending. In recent decades, technological advancements and digital banking have redefined service delivery, enhancing accessibility and efficiency. This study highlights the dynamic evolution of Kerala’s banking system, emphasizing its role in socio-economic development, resilience during financial crises, and adaptation to changing economic landscapes, thereby offering insights into its historical and conte

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: A Study On the Rise of the Gig Economy in Chennai’s Urban Transformation and Its Impact On Employment Patterns
abstract: Urban transformation and digital advancement have significantly reshaped employment patterns in Chennai, leading to the rapid growth of the gig economy. This study examines the impact of gig work on income, job security, and working conditions, and analyses how urban development has contributed to the expansion of gig job opportunities. The research aims to understand the growth of platform-based employment and the challenges faced by gig workers in Chennai’s emerging workforce. The study adopts a descriptive research design. Primary data were collected from 160 respondents using proportionate random sampling across major gig sectors such as transportation, food delivery, logistics, and freelance services. Secondary data were gathered from journals, reports, and official publications. Statistical tools, including percentage analysis, ANOVA, and correlation analysis, were used to test the hypotheses and interpret the data. The findings reveal significant growth of the gig economy in Chennai. ANOVA results show that gig work significantly affects income levels, job security, and working conditions. Correlation analysis indicates a strong positive relationship between urban developmen

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Campus Biodiversity as a Pedagogical Tool:An Experiential Agro-Ecological Study in a School Landscape
abstract: Biodiversity plays a critical role in sustaining agro-ecosystems and ensuring ecological resilience. However, its integration into school-level education remains largely theoretical. This study presents a campus-based biodiversity assessment conducted through an experiential learning framework, with specific emphasis on agro-ecological relevance. The research was carried out within a school campus environment, where students actively participated in site mapping, microhabitat creation, and systematic biodiversity documentation. The study recorded a diverse assemblage of flora and fauna, including herbaceous plants, pollinators, decomposers, and avian species. The introduction of microhabitats significantly enhanced species richness and ecological interactions. The findings demonstrate that even small institutional landscapes can function as micro-agro-ecosystems supporting biodiversity. Additionally, the study highlights the effectiveness of experiential pedagogy in fostering ecological literacy, conservation ethics, and applied environmental understanding. The paper advocates for integrating biodiversity-based experiential learning into education systems to support sustainable agr

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Reconceptualizing Teaching in The Era of Artificial Intelligence: Evidence from Contemporary Research
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing the educational system improving individualized education, elevating the efficiency of teachers, and providing data-driven decision-making. The paper examines the use of AI in instruction, with specific references to adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring, automated grading, predictive analytics, and gamification. It also discusses the practical AI applications like Heuristics-based learning systems, Napkin AI, and NotebookLM, which assist teachers to create, visualize, and organize knowledge. Although AI has important advantages, issues like privacy of data, digital divide, and bias in algorithms have to be curbed to create a fair and ethical practice. The paper presents the conclusion that AI is a partner to teachers and not a substitute, and this technology enhances efficiency, engagement, and innovation in education.

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: From Linguistic Foundations to Literary Art: Exploring the Interdependent Relationship Between Language and Literature Through Statistical Analysis
abstract: This study investigates the intricate connection between language and literature, focusing on the elements that shape literary understanding and reader engagement. It adopts an integrated perspective that merges theoretical linguistics with applied literary analysis, utilizing SPSS statistical tools to examine different aspects of language–literature interaction. The theoretical foundation views language as the earliest system of human communication, while literature is considered a creative and artistic extension built upon that linguistic base. The research highlights how literature reshapes ordinary language into expressive and imaginative forms through metaphor, symbolism, and multilayered meanings that go beyond everyday communication. Works such as Geoffrey Chaucer’s contributions to English writing, Emily Brontë’s vivid natural imagery in Wuthering Heights, and William Blake’s symbolic animal representations demonstrate how authors transform simple words into powerful artistic expressions. Methodologically, the study analyzes variables affecting literary engagement, including native language competence, reading frequency, genre preferences, academic performance, expressive i

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: The Architecture of Dread: Absurdity and Anxiety in The Trial and The Metamorphosis of Franz Kafka
abstract: Franz Kafka’s literary oeuvre occupies a unique position in modern literature, offering narratives that resist definitive interpretation while powerfully articulating the existential anxieties of the twentieth century. This paper examines the intricate relationship between absurdity and anxiety in Kafka’s major works, arguing that his literary project constructs what might be termed an "architecture of dread"—a labyrinthine space where meaning collapses yet the desperate search for meaning persists. Through close analysis of The Metamorphosis and The Trial, to explore how Kafka’s protagonists inhabit worlds governed by incomprehensible rules, pursued by invisible authorities, and consumed by guilt without discernible transgression. The paper further considers Kafka’s relationship to existentialist thought, particularly the philosophical framework later articulated by Albert Camus, while maintaining that Kafka’s vision remains distinct in its refusal to resolve the tension between hope and despair. Ultimately, Kafka’s achievement lies in his ability to render anxiety not merely as psychological condition but as the very structure of modern existence—an existence rendered absurd not

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: An Examination into Optimization Methodologies: Their Applications and Comparative Analysis
abstract: Optimization algorithms exist to find solutions to various problems and then find out the optimal solutions. These algorithms are designed to reach desired goals with high accuracy and low error, as well as improve performance in various fields, including machine learning, operations research, physics, chemistry, and engineering. As technology continues to advance, optimization algorithms are increasingly needed to address complex real-world challenges and drive innovation across all disciplines. Quantitative leaps have been achieved in improving the efficiency of optimization algorithms through the diversity of sources of information feeding these algorithms according to the type of optimization problem, based on scientific and organized foundations. The objectives of this paper are to discuss the most important optimization algorithms, classify the scientific fields involved in their application, and optimize problems involved in this regard, in addition to providing a brief overview for comparison among these algorithms.

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: A TOPSIS-based analysis of Early Modern English:Evaluating linguistic evolution through multiple criteria
abstract: This study examines the linguistic evolution of Early Modern English and uses the TOPSIS method to analyse different linguistic stages. The research examines four main aspects: linguistic development, sociolinguistic context, language standardization, and phonetic changes in five periods: Early Modern English, Renaissance English, Early New English, Pre-Modern English, and Medieval English. Using the TOPSIS method, the study provides a quantitative analysis of these linguistic stages, with each criterion weighted equally at 0.25. The results reveal significant variations in linguistic development across different periods, with Early New English showing the highest normalized values for linguistic development (0.6797) and sociolinguistic context (0.6163). Renaissance English shows the strongest performance in phonetic changes (0.6799), while Early Modern English excels in language standardization (0.7998). The final TOPSIS analysis ranks Medieval English first with a Ci value of 0.6947, followed by Early New English (0.6542), Pre-Modern English (0.5818), Renaissance English (0.5271), and Early Modern English (0.0834). journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Beyond Enrollment: Assessing the Impact of India’s Right to Education Act, 2009 on Learning Outcomes Among Tribal Girls in Deoghar District
abstract: This study examines Impact of the Right to Education Act (RTE) 2009 on the educational outcomes of tribal children tribal girls in Deoghar district of Jharkhand. Despite constitutional promises of universal primary education, tribal communities remain among the most educationally marginalized communities in India. The research analyses four key metrics, namely enrollment rate, attendance rate, government support index and pass percentage, across 500 observations of educational institutions serving tribal girls. Descriptive statistics reveal that the mean enrollment and attendance rates are 70.67% and 75.07% respectively, with a mean pass percentage of 57.76%, indicating moderate overall performance but significant outcome variability (33.33%-81.33%). While enrollment (r=0.68) and attendance (r=0.56) show moderately positive associations with educational performance, the government support index reveals weak correlations (-0.012 to 0.51), indicating that infrastructure and resource provision alone cannot guarantee learning outcomes without improvements in teaching quality. A random forest regression model was developed to predict pass percentage, achieving exceptional accuracy on tr

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: From The Personal to the Political Social Activism in Tamil Cinematic Storytelling
abstract: This study explores the evolution of socially responsible storytelling in Tamil cinema through a comparative analysis of the films of two directors, K. Balachander and Mari Selvaraj, who are united by their commitment to social critique but separated by generations. It contextualizes their works within the socio-political landscapes of Tamil Nadu to understand how cinema functions as a medium for social awareness and reform. Balachander's films from the 1970s, through nuanced, introspective narratives and symbolic storytelling, address middle-class anxieties, gender roles, and ethical conflicts; they emphasize individual struggles within societal structures. In contrast, Mari Selvaraj's contemporary cinema employs a more confrontational and political approach, directly addressing caste oppression, structural violence, and collective resistance. By employing qualitative thematic, narrative, and symbolic analysis within the frameworks of social responsibility theory and cultivation theory, this study reveals a shift in Tamil cinema from individual-centric social inquiry to a more collective political consciousness. This shift reflects the changing sensibilities of the audience and th

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: The Interplay between Emotional Intelligence, Professional Development Engagement, and Teacher Performance
abstract: In the contemporary educational environment, teacher performance is a critical factor influencing student success and institutional effectiveness. Emotional intelligence (EI) and professional development engagement are increasingly recognized as key contributors to teaching effectiveness. This study examines the relationship between emotional intelligence, professional development engagement, and teacher performance among faculty members in Arts and Science colleges in Chennai. A quantitative research design was adopted, and data were collected from 217 teachers using a structured questionnaire through purposive sampling. The data were analysed using SPSS, employing Pearson’s correlation and simple linear regression analyses. The findings reveal a significant positive relationship between emotional intelligence and teacher performance. Further, emotional intelligence was found to significantly predict teachers’ engagement in professional development activities, indicating that emotionally competent teachers are more actively involved in continuous learning. The study highlights the importance of integrating emotional intelligence development with professional development initiative

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: A Framework for the Introduction and Evaluation of Advanced Practice Nursing
abstract: Practice Nursing, Nursing is a noble and essential profession that plays a pivotal role in the healthcare industry. It encompasses a wide range of responsibilities, from providing compassionate care to patients and their families to administering complex medical treatments and advocating for the wellbeing of individuals in times of vulnerability. Nurses are the backbone of healthcare, serving as the bridge between medical expertise and patient needs. In this paragraph, we will delve into the multifaceted nature of nursing practice, exploring the diverse roles nurses play in promoting health, preventing illness, and improving the quality of life for countless individuals. Evidence-Based Practice (EBP): Nursing research provides the foundation for evidence-based practice. EBP involves integrating the best available evidence from research, clinical expertise, and patient preferences to make informed decisions about patient care. By conducting and applying research findings, nurses can ensure that their practice is based on the latest scientific knowledge, leading to better patient outcomes. Improved Patient Care: Nursing research contributes to the development of innovative interventi

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Smart Campus Surveillance and Guidance System Using Face Recognition
abstract: A smart campus surveillance system that uses face recognition technology aims to change how security and administration work in educational institutions. The system captures real-time video from cameras placed around the campus. It compares detected faces to a secure database of registered students, faculty, and staff, which allows for automatic identification and access control. In addition to security, the system helps with attendance tracking by logging recognized individuals without manual input. This reduces the administrative workload and minimizes human error. It can also detect unauthorized personnel, send alert notifications, and provide detailed movement logs for later analysis. This significantly improves the campus's ability to respond to security incidents. The system is built to be scalable and respectful of privacy, allowing it to integrate with existing infrastructure and comply with data protection laws. Real-time analytics and reporting tools provide useful insights for campus administrators. This supports better decision-making about resource use and safety measures. Overall, this face recognition surveillance solution helps create a safer, more efficient, and te

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: AI Based Traffic Management System
abstract: A growing problem for cities around the world is urban traffic congestion, which lowers quality of life, increases pollution, and causes economic losses. Traditional traffic signal systems operate on pre-timed schedules that are often inadequate in responding to real-time traffic fluctuations. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a dynamic alternative through adaptive traffic signal control systems that respond to real-time traffic data, optimize flow, and reduce congestion. The core technologies of AI-based traffic signal control are examined in this paper, with an emphasis on computer vision, reinforcement learning, and machine learning algorithms. Use cases in multimodal traffic management, emergency vehicle prioritisation, and dynamic signal timing are presented. Case studies from smart cities globally demonstrate the effectiveness of AI in reducing congestion and travel time. Ethical considerations, including privacy, accessibility, and algorithmic fairness, are discussed alongside technical challenges such as sensor reliability, system scalability, and integration with legacy infrastructure. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Evaluating Educational Policy and Administration A Weighted Scoring Method Analysis of Performance Dimensions
abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of education policy and management across domains using the Weighted Scoring Method (WSM). The research assesses five key areas of education leadership, education management, education administration, and education planning and general education policy against four critical dimensions: policy effectiveness, equity, and collaboration and student allocation. Each dimension was assigned equal weighting (0.25) to ensure an unbiased analysis. The findings reveal that education planning emerged as the most effective domain with a high priority score (0.72991), showing particular strength in collaboration and equity measures. Education management came in second place (0.70486), showing balanced performance across all dimensions, particularly in policy effectiveness and student allocation. Education leadership came in third place (0.56527), showing strong performance in equity but needing improvement in collaboration. Public education policy ranked fourth (0.55337), showing strengths in policy performance but weaknesses in student allocation. Educational administration ranked last (0.40102), indicating the need for comprehensive improvements despite ad

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Earthquake History of Assam and Its Geological Record within Some Sedimentary Structures in Upper Assam
abstract: The geology of Assam has played a significant role in the occurrence of notable earthquakes in the region. In a broad regional geological point of view the Assam Arakan basin is within the tectonically active region with the presence of the triple plate junction and there are many records of major earthquakes with a magnitude of above 7 in Richter scale. Major earthquakes in Assam are caused by intense tectonic activity from the collision of the Indian Plate with Eurasian & Burmese plates, creating numerous active faults like the Kopili Fault, Himalayan Frontal Thrust (HFT), and Main Boundary Thrust (MBT), placing the region in the highest seismic zone (Zone V) and making it highly vulnerable. The complex interaction along these fault lines, coupled with the region's geological setting, results in frequent seismic events. Along with a thorough review of available archival records in this study an attempt has been made to explain geologically the earthquake induced structures found within Quaternary deposits of Upper Assam.

journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Happiness level of college teachers in relation to their Self-esteem and Professional ethics
abstract: Happiness is a fundamental human aspiration and plays a vital role in professional effectiveness, especially in the teaching profession, which demands dedication, responsibility, and ethical commitment. The present study examines the happiness level of college teachers in relation to their self-esteem and professional ethics, with special reference to undergraduate colleges in Jorhat district. A descriptive survey method was adopted for the study. The sample consisted of 70 college teachers, selected using simple random sampling for institutions and incidental sampling for teachers. Data were collected using standardized tools, namely the Subjective Happiness Scale, the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, and the Teachers’ Professional Ethics Scale. Statistical techniques such as mean, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, critical ratio, and Pearson’s correlation coefficient were used for analysis. The results reveal that college teachers possess high levels of happiness, self-esteem, and professional ethics. title: Impact of AI-Driven Social Media Marketing on Food Delivery Preferences in Chennai
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a central force shaping how consumers discover and engage with food delivery services, particularly in fast-growing metropolitan environments such as Chennai. This study examines how AI‑driven social media marketing influences food delivery preferences among consumers in Chennai. With food delivery platforms rapidly expanding in India, understanding how algorithmic recommendations, personalized advertisements, and AI‑generated influencer content affect decision‑making has become crucial. A sample of 110 respondents across Chennai participated in the survey. Findings reveal that consumers are increasingly shaped by AI‑filtered content, especially through hyper‑personalized ads and influencer‑driven promotions. Younger audiences demonstrate heightened responsiveness to visually appealing AI‑generated images, real‑time discount notifications, and curated recommendations. Gender emerged as a significant factor, with female respondents reporting higher influence levels. title: Prospects and Problems of Historical Tourism in Sivasagar District, Assam
abstract: Tourism is one of the largest and fastest-growing industries in the world, with enormous potential for further expansion. Each year, approximately 700 million tourists—about 6 percent of the global population—cross international borders. Today, "tourism" encompasses all the relationships and phenomena that arise from travel and the temporary stay of people in unfamiliar places. Factors such as rapid urbanization, rising living standards, the shift of individuals away from rural environments, and increasing leisure time have all contributed to the global development of tourism. The sustained growth of the tourism industry has become a major source of funding for sustainable community development, job creation, the conservation of cultural heritage, and the establishment of diverse cultural identities. The world increasingly recognizes tourism as a significant industry that generates vast business opportunities, creates wealth, acts as an income multiplier, stimulates employment, and helps preserve both culture and the environment. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: ICT Integration and Library Service Transformation An Evaluation of Academic Libraries under Bangalore University and Bengaluru City University
abstract: In the digital era, Information and Communication Technology (ICT) has become an essential component of academic library development, redefining how knowledge is organized, preserved, and accessed. This study explores the extent and effectiveness of ICT integration in college libraries affiliated with Bangalore University and Bengaluru City University, focusing on how digital tools have transformed library services and user experiences. A total of 40 librarians and 180 library users, including faculty members and students, participated in the study through structured questionnaires, interviews, and field visits. The results reveal that ICT adoption has considerably strengthened library functions such as cataloguing, circulation, digital resource sharing, and user support services. However, variations in infrastructure, internet bandwidth, and administrative support were evident across institutions. Libraries under Bangalore University showed more advanced implementation of automation software and online access facilities, whereas several colleges affiliated with Bengaluru City University continue to rely on semi-automated systems due to limited technical and financial resources. journal_name: Journal on Innovations in Teaching & Learning
title: Sustainability Accounting and Reporting Consistency, Comparability, and Assurance
abstract: This study explores the application of algorithm-based analysis in the field of accounting and auditing, with a specific focus on understanding the relationship between input and output parameters. Using expenses, assets, and profit as input parameters and revenue as the output parameter, the research demonstrates how algorithmic approaches can enhance accuracy, efficiency, and predictive power in financial analysis. The findings highlight the growing relevance of computational methods in supporting decision-making processes and improving the reliability of financial reporting. Research Significance: The significance of this research lies in its contribution to bridging the gap between traditional accounting practices and modern technological advancements. By integrating algorithmic analysis into accounting and auditing processes, organizations can better forecast financial outcomes, reduce human error, and strengthen transparency. Additionally, this study emphasizes the practical implications of artificial intelligence and data-driven models in transforming conventional accounting methodologies into more robust, automated systems that support sustainable growth and competitiveness

title: AI-Driven Visual Content Creation in Digital Media Platforms
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed the landscape of digital media by enhancing the processes of visual content creation and media management. AI-driven technologies such as machine learning, computer vision, and deep learning enable the automated generation, editing, and optimization of visual media including images, videos, and graphics. Digital media platforms increasingly rely on AI tools to improve production efficiency, personalize content, and enhance audience engagement. AI-based systems can analyse user preferences, generate creative visuals, and automate repetitive production tasks, allowing media professionals to focus on strategic and creative aspects of content development. Despite these advantages, the integration of AI in visual content creation also raises concerns related to ethical issues, originality, algorithmic bias, and the potential impact on creative employment. title: Role of the Ahom Princes in the Early Anti-British Uprising in Assam with Special Reference to Peali Phukan
abstract: The decline of the glorious six hundred (1228-1826) ruler of the Ahom Dynasty in upper Assam of the Brahmaputra valley finally paved the way for the establishment of the permanent British colonial rule. As compared to other native Indian states, the Ahom kingdom was annexed by the British quite late. From this point of view, the people of Assam, to some extent, escaped from British exploitation. However, from the very beginning of British rule in Assam, they systematically exploited the people of Assam, which was not easily tolerated by the Aristocratic classes, who enjoyed unlimited power and legitimate rights during the time of Ahom rule. The prevailing discontentment of the people of the noble class ultimately paved the way for the early anti-British uprising which shocked the very foundation of British rule in Assam. Most of the Ahom princes lost their lives because of their native land. In this regard, Peali Phukon and Jeuram Dulia Boruah, the first myrtle of the Indian national movement, may be mentioned.
